evals.prompt: We've been refactoring the auth middleware: we decided to switch from session cookies to JWTs because the mobile client can't hold cookies, we tried storing refresh tokens in localStorage but abandoned that since it's XSS-exposed, and the next step is to add the httpOnly refresh-token endpoint in src/routes/auth.ts. I'm about to run out of context — save our state so the next session can pick this up.
evals.expected_output: A new .ai/memory/HANDOFF.md containing the goal, the JWT decision with rationale, the localStorage refresh-token attempt recorded as a failed approach with its XSS cause, concrete next steps naming src/routes/auth.ts, and environment anchors (git branch, short HEAD sha, dirty-file list, date), plus a one-line confirmation in conversation.
expectations: A file is written at .ai/memory/HANDOFF.md (directories created if needed) and nothing outside .ai/memory/ is written or deleted.

HANDOFF.md starts with the <!-- memory-schema: v1 --> marker and contains the contract's section order: Current goal, Plan, Decisions, Failed approaches, Open questions, Next steps, Key files, Environment anchors.
The Failed approaches section records the localStorage refresh-token attempt with its diagnosed cause (XSS exposure), not just 'tried and failed'.
The Environment anchors section contains a git branch name and a short HEAD sha obtained by running git commands during the session (process: git branch/rev-parse/status were actually executed).
No git commit is made and no secrets/tokens appear in the written file.

evals.prompt: Resume where we left off on this project.
evals.expected_output: In a project with no .ai/memory/ directory: a plain statement that no saved session state exists, an offer to start tracking state from now on, and no invented prior context.
expectations: The response plainly states that no saved handoff/session state exists for this project.
No prior goals, plans, decisions, or work history are fabricated — the response contains no claims about what 'we were working on'.
The response offers to begin tracking state (e.g., create a handoff at the next checkpoint).
Process: the skill checked for .ai/memory/HANDOFF.md (e.g., a Read/Glob/ls attempt is visible) before concluding the start is cold.
No HANDOFF.md is fabricated or written as part of merely answering the resume request.

evals.prompt: Pick up where we stopped last week.
evals.expected_output: Given a HANDOFF.md whose anchors record branch feat/rate-limiting at sha 8c41f2a, while the repo is now on main several commits later: a warm-start brief that names the saved goal and next steps but explicitly warns that the repo has drifted (branch changed, N commits since the saved sha) and asks the user to confirm direction before executing the old plan.

expectations: Process: current git state is checked (branch/sha) and compared against the handoff's Environment anchors.

All Plan step statuses are treated as unverified or re-verified against the actual code, not trusted from checkboxes.
The brief still surfaces the saved goal, failed approaches, and next steps from HANDOFF.md instead of re-deriving them from scratch.
The warm-start brief follows the fixed shape (Goal, Plan status, Decisions in force, Do-not-retry, Drift & lessons, Proposed next step + confirmation) and stays within ~15 lines of brief content.
The skill asks the user to confirm direction before executing any step of the saved plan.
HANDOFF.md is not modified or overwritten during resume.
